In cases where parasites reproduce within red blood cells forming groups of four—a formation reminiscent of the Maltese cross, a symbol linked to the Crusades—the primary differential diagnosis considered is malaria. This is because the morphological appearance of parasites, despite being typical for babesiosis, leads clinicians to differentiate it from the well‐known presentation of malaria.
